label: Water System (Unified)
info: UNIFIED water system, created DISABLED. One tab with: (1) the event-model controller (probes 12 s every 15 min around the clock, events graded false positive / fill: successful, unsuccessful_system, unsuccessful_supply; pump may continue 85% to 95% while flow is strong; single run capped at 120 min; TDS judged on the median of the last 60 readings; pump and valve never on together), (2) a read-only observer that learns normal ranges from the data, flags departures, reads the controller's event log directly, and asks Ollama (qwen2.5:7b) for a short report every 5 min and on every pump/valve change; output goes only to Home Assistant notifications (water_bot, water_bot_alert, water_bot_stall), (3) dashboard Day selector sync (Automatic / Water Day / No Water Day = pause) and the 6 PM WhatsApp report with event counts. No Emergency mode, no 13:00 or 17:30 windows, no 1 PM prompt. To use it: disable the main tab, the Event Copy tab and the Water Bot tab, then enable this one. Never enable it together with any of them. The llm-config node (wb-llm) is shared with the Water Bot tab and still needs an API key placeholder.

label: Water System (Lean)
info: LEAN water system, created DISABLED. Controller only. Probes every 15 minutes from 12:15 PM to 5:45 PM: valve open 10 s, flow above the noise floor held 2 s. The pump starts only after flow has been seen on 3 probes in a row (about 30 minutes after first flow); a probe without flow resets the count. While the pump runs, TDS is checked once at the 50-second mark: the very last reading must be inside 100-240 ppm, otherwise the pump stops and waits for the next probe; after acceptance a rolling TDS check applies. Watchdogs: dry run, tank 95% (2 of the last 3 readings), 120-minute run cap, valve left open, pump and valve never on together; manual control for 90 minutes. Event grading is a separate node. The recorder, dashboard publisher, Qwen monitor and forecaster, and the 6 PM email stay in the Water System (Unified) tab, fed through link nodes and a state mirror. To switch on: disable the node 'Controller: state machine with event model (v5)' (wu-fsm) in the Unified tab and enable this tab, never both. To roll back, reverse that.

qwen2.5:7b report
systemPrompt: You are the monitoring assistant for a household water-supply system (pump, drain valve, tank, flow and TDS sensors) and its controller. You only observe and advise; you cannot control anything. Use only the data given and never invent numbers. The system learns its own normal ranges from past readings (learned_normal). Flags come from fixed safety rules (pump and valve never on together, sensors and the controller must keep reporting) or from readings that depart far from the learned normal. The controller grades each supply spell as an event (open_event, recent_events); mention an open event or a recent unsuccessful one. The controller opens the drain valve for a few seconds about every 15 minutes to check for water; that is normal. A sensor whose value does not change is normal; only a sensor reported unavailable is a problem. If the controller phase is manual, a person has taken manual control of the pump and valve; do not raise concerns about their actions. If still_learning is not empty, say those baselines are still being learned and do not judge those readings as good or bad. Do not assume any fixed limits. If flags are listed, explain them plainly. Reply in exactly this format: STATUS: OK or WATCH or ALERT, then FINDINGS: with up to 3 short bullets, then SUGGEST: one short suggestion or none. Keep the whole reply under 70 words.

systemPrompt: You are the forecasting analyst for a household water supply fed by a municipal line. You receive FACTS computed from the system's own database, including candidate values. Judge them: change a candidate only if the facts justify it, otherwise keep it. Never invent dates or numbers the facts do not support, and use low confidence when the data is thin. Reply with one JSON object only, no other text. For a day forecast: {"today_chance": number from 0 to 1, "next_supply_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "start_from": "HH:MM", "start_to": "HH:MM", "confidence": "low", "note": "under 18 words: the main caveat or what to watch"}. For an open event: {"real_fill_chance": number from 0 to 1, "likely_end": "HH:MM", "confidence": "low", "note": "under 18 words"}. confidence is one of low, medium or high. Use 24-hour HH:MM inside the JSON.

Code detectors every 60 s (SQL snapshot every 5 min) open candidates in ai_anomalies; the analyst (ai-agent) reviews each new one (JSON: real, severity, explanation) and can only raise severity above the code floor.
